# Nomikos

> AI-assisted annotation platform for historical manuscripts. Models draft segments and transcriptions. Researchers review and edit. Open HTR models on Hugging Face. Part of the NOMOS research ecosystem.

Nomikos is open research tooling for manuscript HTR workflows: page annotation, model-assisted transcription, local or cloud inference, and export of training-ready line data.

## Site

- [Home](https://nomikos.app/): Product overview, demo videos, features, and published models
- [App](https://app.nomikos.app/): Hosted annotation platform
- [llms.txt](https://nomikos.app/llms.txt): This file

## Models

- [greek-htr-calamari](https://huggingface.co/nomikos-project/greek-htr-calamari): Byzantine Greek line HTR (Calamari), published. Model card reports CER 0.156 on validation (19 lines) and 0.226 on test (21 lines)
- [armenian-htr-calamari](https://huggingface.co/nomikos-project/armenian-htr-calamari): Armenian line HTR (Calamari), published. Model card reports CER 0.092 on validation (119 lines) and 0.072 on test (120 lines)
- [syriac-htr-ppocr_rec](https://huggingface.co/nomikos-project/syriac-htr-ppocr_rec): Syriac line HTR (PP-OCR recognition), published. Authors report test CER about 0.07
- [coptic-htr-calamari](https://huggingface.co/nomikos-project/coptic-htr-calamari): Coptic line HTR (Calamari), published. Model card reports CER 0.082 on test (283 lines)
- [greek-manuscript-htr](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nomikos-project/greek-manuscript-htr): Byzantine Greek HTR dataset, BnF Grec 1360. 5 pages, 204 lines
- [armenian-manuscript-htr](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nomikos-project/armenian-manuscript-htr): Armenian HTR dataset, BnF Arménien 172 and UCLA Armenian MS 72. 34 pages, 1,704 lines
- [syriac-manuscript-htr](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nomikos-project/syriac-manuscript-htr): East Syriac HTR dataset, Alqosh 65. 7 pages, 143 lines
- [Author models on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/nomikos-project): Published checkpoints

Reported CER figures come from held-out packs on specific manuscripts. The Armenian and Coptic packs run to a few hundred lines each; the Greek test pack holds 21 lines, so its figure is much noisier. None of it is a platform-wide accuracy guarantee: CER moves with the script, the hand, image quality, layout, and the training data behind the checkpoint.
